Vide this judgment, this Court shall decide and dispose off the present eviction petition filed by the petitioners under Section 14 (1) (e) of DRC Act against the respondent Sh. Chander Mohan, S/o- Sh. Rishi Ram (hereinafter as the respondent) seeking his eviction from the tenanted premises on Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 1 the ground of bonafide requirement. 3. The bonafide requirement of the petitioners is that they need the tenanted premises for the storage of goods for the business of their father Sh. Sat Parkash. 4. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners, as per their petition, are as follows:- i) That the tenanted shop was let out by Late Sh. Chander Bhan (i.e. the grandfather of the petitioners) to the respondent for non-residential purposes w.e.f. 01.08.1996, for running business therein. It is stated that the tenancy was oral accompanied with possession. iii) That the grandfather of the petitioners namely Sh. Chander Bhan died on 10.06.2015, leaving behind him a registered Will dated 27.05.2002 bequeathing property No.223, Gali No.9, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi-110007 to the petitioners. iv) That thereafter the petitioners have become the owner of the entire property No.223, Gali No.9, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi-110007, including the tenanted shop i.e. the tenanted premises. It is stated that by operation of law, the respondent became tenant under the petitioners and no lease deed was executed between the parties. It is stated that the tenancy of the respondent is a month to month basis tenancy commencing on the first day of the month and expiring on the last day of the month and at present the rate of rent is Rs.1150/- per month excluding other charges. v) It is averred that the earlier the respondent used to carry on his business of general store in the tenanted premises, however, from the last about one year the respondent has shifted his aforesaid business from the tenanted premises to property bearing No.231/2, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi, which is being used by the respondent for keeping goods of his business. vi) That the petitioners bonafidely require the tenanted shop for storage of goods of the business of their father namely Sh. Sat Parkash, who has been running a shop of sale of all types of stationary goods in the adjoining shop, as shown in blue colour in the site plan attached to the petition; neither the petitioners nor their father have got any other reasonably suitable accommodation with them for the abovesaid purpose. vi) That earlier the father of the petitioners used to store goods of his aforesaid business in a room situated on the ground floor of property No.224/2B, Gali No.7, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi- 110007; the said property belongs to the brother of the father of the petitioners namely Sh. Jai Parkash as well as to the wife and two sons of Sh. Brahm Parkash, who was the elder brother of Sh. Sat Parkash. vii) That the son of late Sh. Brahm Parkash namely Sh. Nitin, who is aged about 27 years, has been running a shop of general store in a shop situated on the ground floor of the property No.223, Gali Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 2 No.9, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi-110007 since March, 2015, as specifically shown in yellow colour in the site plan. The possession of the said shop was obtained by the grandfather of the petitioners pursuance to the eviction order dated 02.05.2013 passed against the respondent Sh. Ram Babu by the court of Sh. Parveen Singh, the then Ld. ARC, Central, Tis Hazari Court. viii) That Sh. Nitin, after started running business in the shop mentioned above, had started living in the property No.224/2B, Gali No.7, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi-110007 and had also started storing goods of his business in the room situated on the ground floor of the aforesaid property, in which room, earlier the father of the petitioners used to keep goods of his business. ix) That thereafter the father of the petitioners had started keeping goods of his business in the room and covered verandah on the first floor of property No.223, Gali No.9, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj-110007, which are marked by letters X and X-1 in the site plan. x) It is submitted that there are two rooms and covered verandah on the first floor of the property No.223, Gali No.9, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj-110007 and the petitioners alongwith their father and one sister, who is aged about 20 years, have been residing on the first floor of abovesaid property. xi) That the petitioner no.1 is pursuing C.A. course from Delhi and the petitioner no.2 is doing ITI course from Jail Road, New Delhi. It is stated after the father of the petitioners vacated the room in property No.224/2B, Gali No.7, Padam Nagar, Kishan Ganj, Delhi-110007, where he was storing goods of his business, the petitioners have been feeling great difficulty in living on the first floor of the tenanted property inasmuch as the accommodation available on the tenanted premises is not sufficient for the residence of the petitioners and their father. Hence, it is stated that the tenanted shop is bonafidely required by the petitioners for storage of goods of the business of their father. xii) It is, therefore, prayed that an eviction order may be passed in favour of the petitioners and against the respondent in respect of the tenanted premises. 5. On the receipt of notice of the petition in the form prescribed in the third Schedule of DRC Act, the respondent appeared before the Court and applied for leave to defend. The said liberty was granted to the respondent by the Ld. Predecessor of this court vide order dated 15.12.2017, and thereafter, a written statement was filed on behalf of the respondent. He has relied upon the documents i.e. photographs of the shop, as shown in yellow colour in the site plan, of different dates, which are Ex.PW1/R1 and Ex.RW1/R11. 16. RW-1 was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for the petitioners.

It is submitted that the father of the petitioner is carrying on his business of the stationary items to a limited extent on a small level which does not require any storage space as is being alleged in the petition. It is submitted that no photograph has been filed by the petitioner on record to show that any room is occupied by the father of the petitioners in the abovesaid property. vii) it is averred that the brother of the present respondent has already been evicted and now the petitioners by putting up a case of requirement of their father are trying to evict the respondent from the tenanted premises. viii) It is denied that Sh. Counsel further submitted that the projected need is that the tenanted premises is required for the business of father of the petitioner, who is running a retail shop of stationary items and in order to claim additional space/shop, it was incumbent upon him to show that there has been an expansion in his business, however, despite opportunity the same has not been done and thus the need cannot be called bonafide. iii) In support of this submission, the Ld. Counsel had drawn the attention of the court to the testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 and had argued that the said two witnesses have admitted that there is no expansion. iv) The second ground/defence agitated by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent was that the petitioners are in possession of an alternate accommodation which is a shop, as shown in yellow colour in the site plan filed by the petitioners Ex.PW1/1. It is argued that the said shop was lying unused at the time of the filing of the present petition, however, now it has been put to use by relative of the petitioners Nitin. He had drawn the attention of the court towards compromise arrived at between the then grandfather of the petitioner Late Sh. Chander Bhan who was earlier the owner of the suit property, by which the shop which was in the tenancy of the brother of the respondent was got vacated from him and in the said shop Nitin had established his business and in pursuance to the same the room which was in another property owned by the father of Nitin and uncle of Nitin was handed over to the brother of the respondent and after start of business Nitin has started keeping goods/business in the rooms in the other property. This room was earlier being used by the father of the petitioners for keeping goods of the stationary business and in these circumstances the father of the petitioner had vacated the said room on the ground floor and has started keeping goods of business on the first floor of the suit property, which is residential. It was argued that the space available on the first floor of the suit property is not even sufficient for the residential purpose of the petitioners and his family members and as such the present petition has been filed for the bonafide requirement of the father of the petitioners for keeping goods/business in the tenanted premises. 19. 20. Additionally, it has been argued on behalf of the respondent that the father of the petitioner is not dependent upon him and as such a stationary shop does not require storage, thus the projected need is only fictional. Lastly, Ld. Counsel for the respondent argued that it has not been shown that the father of the petitioner ever used any additional space, which is averred to have been given to their relative and hence the requirement is not bonafide. 21. The present petition is an eviction petition filed under Section 14 (1)(e) of DRC Act, whereby the petitioner is seeking eviction of the tenant on the ground of bonafide need. It reads as under;- "14. Protection of tenant against eviction, - (1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law or contract, no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made by and court or Controller in favor of the landlord against a tenant: Provided that the Controller may, on an application made to him in the prescribed manner, make an order for the recovery of possession of the premises on one or more of the following grounds only, namely:- (a) *** Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 8 (b)*** (c)*** (d)*** (e) That the premises are required bona fide by the landlord for himself or for any member of his family dependent on him, if he is the owner thereof, or for any person for whose benefit the premises are held and the landlord or such person has no other reasonably suitable accommodation; Explanation.- For the purpose of this clause, "premises let for residential purpose" include any premises which having been let for use as a residence are, without the consent of the landlord, used incidentally for commercial or other purposes;" 22. In order to establish the grounds for eviction of the tenant/respondent under section 14(1)(e) of the DRC Act, the petitioner must establish the following essentials, viz. i) Landlord - tenant relationship between the parties; and ii) Petitioner requires the premises bonafide for himself, or for any member of his family dependent upon him; and iii) That the petitioner does not have any other reasonable alternate suitable accommodation. 29. The full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh distinguished between the genuine requirement and the reasonable requirement. It was held in case of Damodar Sharma & Anr. Vs. Nandram Deviram that: "It is wrong to say that "genuinely requires" is the same as "reasonably requires." There is distinction between the two phrases. The former phrase refers to a state of mind; the later to an objective standard. "Genuine requirement" would vary according to the idiosyncrasy of the individual and the time and circumstances in which he lives and thinks. Reasonable requirement belong to the "knowledge of the law" and means reasonable not in the mind of the person requiring the accommodation but reasonable according to the actual facts. In the matter at hand, the need projected by the petitioner is that the father of the petitioner requires the tenanted premises in question as storage space for his already existing stationary business. It has been averred by the petitioners that the father of the petitioner is occupying a portion of the residential premises, at the first floor, to satisfy the existing need, however, the same is creating an undue hardship for the other family member. 31. Whereas the respondents have not denied that the father of the petitioner is already engaged in stationary business, it is disputed that he has any further requirement i.e. the tenanted premises in question is needed for additional storage. It is the argument of the respondents that a stationary business is not something which requires a godown in the background. Especially considering the fact that the petitioner's father is a retailer, as per the respondents, the additional storage is unwarranted and the same is being fictionally pleaded, only to get the tenanted premises in question vacated. As per the respondents over the years, the business of father of the petitioner has not seen any exponential growth and therefore the projected requirement is sham. Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 10 32. Per contra, the petitioner's case is that with passage of time, the stationary business has seen changes such as that a photocopy machine, the facility of print-out etc. was introduced. Therefore, there is a requirement for expansion.s 33. Ld. Counsel for the petitioners argued that merely because the petitioner's father does not file any income tax (as he is in non-taxable bracket), it cannot be construed that his requirement is fictional. 36. In the considered opinion of this Court, the respondents failed to point any material inconsistencies etc. in the course of the cross-examination of the petitioner's witnesses and therefore this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner has successfully pleaded that the need projected by him is bonafide. In Jagdish Chand Gulati VS. Kanta Devi, 1996 (36) DRJ 654, it was held that the court has to take into consideration the facts which exist at the time of passing of the judgment. Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 12 43. Reference is made to the judgment in J.L. Mehta Vs. Smt. Hira Devi, 1970 DLT 484 = 1971 RCJ 272. 46.

Vishal Anr vs Chander Mohan on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116669702/ 12 43. Reference is made to the judgment in J.L. Mehta Vs. Smt. Hira Devi, 1970 DLT 484 = 1971 RCJ 272. 46.
